title: LSASS Memory Dumped via Comsvcs
description: Detects the comsvcs.dll MiniDump technique, which abuses a signed Windows binary to write LSASS memory to disk without dropping a credential-dumping tool.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Diagnostic memory dumps created by support tools

title: Linux Reverse Shell Command
description: Detects common reverse-shell one-liners that redirect a shell to a remote address. The pattern is rare in normal server operations and should be treated as active intrusion.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Debugging sessions by a platform engineer
query_kql: process.command_line:(*\/dev\/tcp\/* OR *bash\ \-i* OR *nc\ \-e* OR *ncat\ \-e* OR *socat\ exec*)

title: Ransomware Note Dropped on Disk
description: Detects common ransom note filenames written by encryptors. A note alone is not proof of encryption, so analysts should pivot on file writes and recovery deletion.
author: Meruyert

title: SAM or SECURITY Hive Dumped with Reg.exe
description: Detects reg.exe saving the SAM, SECURITY, or SYSTEM hive. Those files contain local password hashes and are commonly copied off-host for offline cracking.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Backup tools that export registry hives
Forensic acquisition performed by an incident responder
query: any where (process.executable.caseless:"*\\reg.exe" and process.command_line:"*save*") and (process.command_line like~ ("*hklm\\sam*", "*hklm\\security*", "*hklm\\system*"))

title: Suspicious Process Access to LSASS
description: Detects a non-standard process opening LSASS with credential-dumping access rights. Covers common tooling patterns (mimikatz, procdump, comsvcs.dll minidump) while excluding known security products and Windows components.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Endpoint protection and EDR agents reading process memory
query: any where winlog.channel:"Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" and ((event.code:"10" and winlog.event_data.TargetImage:"*\\lsass.exe" and (winlog.event_data.GrantedAccess like~ ("0x1010", "0x1410", "0x1438", "0x143a", "0x1fffff"))) and (not (process.executable.caseless like~ ("*\\MsMpEng.exe", "*\\MpCmdRun.exe", "*\\svchost.exe", "*\\csrss.exe"))))
query_kql: winlog.channel:Microsoft\-Windows\-Sysmon\/Operational AND (winlog.channel:Microsoft\-Windows\-Sysmon\/Operational AND ((event.code:10 AND winlog.event_data.TargetImage:*\\lsass.exe AND (winlog.event_data.GrantedAccess:(0x1010 OR 0x1410 OR 0x1438 OR 0x143a OR 0x1fffff))) AND (NOT (process.executable.caseless:(*\\MsMpEng.exe OR *\\MpCmdRun.exe OR *\\svchost.exe OR *\\csrss.exe)))))

title: AMSI Bypass via Reflection
description: Detects PowerShell that tampers with the Antimalware Scan Interface through reflection. Attackers use this to run known malicious scripts without content inspection.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Some legitimate PowerShell modules that probe AMSI state

title: Boot Recovery Disabled via BCDEdit
description: Detects changes that disable Windows recovery or ignore boot failures, which attackers use to keep a host from booting into repair mode after encryption.
author: Meruyert
query: any where (process.executable.caseless:"*\\bcdedit.exe" and (process.command_line:"*recoveryenabled*" and process.command_line:"*no*")) or (process.executable.caseless:"*\\bcdedit.exe" and (process.command_line:"*bootstatuspolicy*" and process.command_line:"*ignoreallfailures*"))
query_kql: (process.executable.caseless:*\\bcdedit.exe AND (process.command_line:*recoveryenabled* AND process.command_line:*no*)) OR (process.executable.caseless:*\\bcdedit.exe AND (process.command_line:*bootstatuspolicy* AND process.command_line:*ignoreallfailures*))

title: Certutil Used to Download or Decode a Payload
description: Detects certutil.exe invoked with urlcache, verifyctl or decode switches. Certutil is a signed Windows binary commonly abused to download or decode attacker tooling while blending in with legitimate administration.
author: Meruyert

title: Cloud Access Key Created
description: Detects creation of a new cloud access key. Attackers create keys after taking over an identity so they can return without the original password.
author: Meruyert

title: Cloud Root Account Console Login
description: Detects a successful console login by the cloud root account. Routine work should use named identities, so root use warrants review.
author: Meruyert
query: any where event.action:"ConsoleLogin" and user.name:"root" and event.outcome:"success"

title: Command Injection Attempt in Web Request
description: Detects shell metacharacters and download commands in web parameters. These payloads attempt to turn a web request into operating-system execution.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Application features that legitimately accept shell syntax
query: any where url.query like~ ("*;wget*", "*|bash*", "*$(*", "*`id`*", "*&& curl*", "*; curl*")
query_kql: url.query:(*;wget* OR *\|bash* OR *$\(* OR *`id`* OR *\&\&\ curl* OR *;\ curl*)

title: Critical Service Stopped Before Impact
description: Detects stop events for backup, database, and endpoint protection services. Ransomware operators stop these services first so files are not locked and backups cannot be restored during encryption.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Administrators stopping a service during maintenance
Backup jobs that cycle the agent service
query: any where winlog.channel:"System" and (event.code:"7036" and (winlog.event_data.ServiceName like~ ("VSS", "SQLSERVERAGENT", "MSSQLSERVER", "BackupExecAgentBrowser", "WinDefend", "Sense")))
query_kql: winlog.channel:System AND (winlog.channel:System AND (event.code:7036 AND (winlog.event_data.ServiceName:(VSS OR SQLSERVERAGENT OR MSSQLSERVER OR BackupExecAgentBrowser OR WinDefend OR Sense))))

title: Cron Job Executing Remote Content
description: Detects cron invoking a shell that pipes remote content into an interpreter. This pattern is a common way to establish recurring access on Linux hosts.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Legitimate maintenance jobs that fetch installer scripts

title: Kerberoasting Service Ticket Request
description: Detects service ticket requests with RC4 encryption, a common Kerberoasting pattern. Analysts should check whether the requesting account normally asks for that service.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Legacy applications that still require RC4 service tickets
query: any where winlog.channel:"Security" and ((event.code:"4769" and winlog.event_data.TicketEncryptionType:"0x17") and (not service.name:"*$"))
query_kql: winlog.channel:Security AND (winlog.channel:Security AND ((event.code:4769 AND winlog.event_data.TicketEncryptionType:0x17) AND (NOT service.name:*$)))

title: Large Outbound Network Transfer
description: Detects a single outbound flow larger than 10 MB. The threshold is deliberately high so normal browsing and updates do not dominate the queue.
author: Meruyert

title: Linux Log File Tampering
description: Detects deletion or truncation of system logs. Removing auth or syslog data is a deliberate defense-evasion step.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Log rotation scripts that use truncate

title: Mshta Executing Remote or Script Content
description: Detects mshta.exe loading a remote URL or inline script. Mshta is a signed binary that can execute VBScript or JScript outside the browser sandbox.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Legacy line-of-business applications built on HTA

title: Office Application Spawns a Shell
description: Detects Word, Excel, or Outlook starting a command interpreter or script host. This parent-child pair is a strong signal of a malicious macro.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Office add-ins that launch a signed helper process
query_kql: (process.parent.executable.caseless:(*\\WINWORD.EXE OR *\\EXCEL.EXE OR *\\OUTLOOK.EXE OR *\\POWERPNT.EXE)) AND (process.executable.caseless:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\mshta.exe))

title: PHP File Uploaded to Web Accessible Directory
description: Detects an HTTP POST to a .php path inside a writable or upload directory. A successful upload of executable PHP content is a strong indicator of web shell deployment, the most common way attackers persist on a web server.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Applications that legitimately accept PHP file uploads (rare, should be reviewed)
query: any where http.request.method:"POST" and url.path:"*.php" and (url.path like~ ("*/upload*", "*/uploads/*", "*/images/*", "*/tmp/*", "*/files/*"))
query_kql: http.request.method:POST AND url.path:*.php AND (url.path:(*\/upload* OR *\/uploads\/* OR *\/images\/* OR *\/tmp\/* OR *\/files\/*))

title: PowerShell Download Cradle
description: Detects PowerShell that downloads and executes content in one expression. The pattern is common in phishing payloads and commodity loaders.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Software deployment scripts that download installers
query_kql: (process.executable.caseless:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe)) AND (process.command_line:(*DownloadString* OR *DownloadFile* OR *Invoke\-WebRequest* OR *Net.WebClient* OR *IEX\(* OR *Invoke\-Expression*))

title: PowerShell Encoded Command Execution
description: Detects PowerShell or pwsh started with an encoded command switch. Adversaries use base64-encoded commands to obfuscate payloads and evade string-based command line detection.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Software deployment tools that wrap scripts in encoded commands (SCCM, Intune)
Administrators running pre-built encoded onboarding scripts
query: any where (process.executable.caseless like~ ("*\\powershell.exe", "*\\pwsh.exe")) and (process.command_line like~ ("* -enc *", "* -encodedcommand *", "* -ec *", "* -e JAB*")) and (not (process.parent.executable.caseless like~ ("*\\ccmexec.exe", "*\\Microsoft.ConfigurationManagement.exe")))
query_kql: (process.executable.caseless:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe)) AND (process.command_line:(*\ \-enc\ * OR *\ \-encodedcommand\ * OR *\ \-ec\ * OR *\ \-e\ JAB*)) AND (NOT (process.parent.executable.caseless:(*\\ccmexec.exe OR *\\Microsoft.ConfigurationManagement.exe)))

title: PsExec Service Creation
description: Detects the PSEXESVC service that PsExec installs on a remote host. This is a reliable signal of remote execution with stolen administrative credentials.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Administrators using PsExec for legitimate remote support
Some backup and deployment tools embed PSEXESVC
query: any where winlog.channel:"System" and (event.code:"7045" and winlog.event_data.ImagePath:"*PSEXESVC*")

title: Registry Run Key Persistence
description: Detects writes to per-user or machine Run keys that point at user-writable paths or scripting engines. Run keys survive reboot and need no service install.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Software installers that register a startup entry
query_kql: registry.path:*\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\* AND (winlog.event_data.Details:(*\\Users\\Public\\* OR *\\AppData\\Roaming\\* OR *powershell* OR *cmd.exe* OR *mshta*))

title: Rundll32 or Regsvr32 Remote Payload
description: Detects signed Windows binaries loading script or remote content. Rundll32 and Regsvr32 are trusted by users and often missed by application allowlists.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Legacy installers that register COM components from a URL
query: any where (process.executable.caseless:"*\\rundll32.exe" and (process.command_line like~ ("*javascript:*", "*http://*", "*https://*"))) or (process.executable.caseless:"*\\regsvr32.exe" and (process.command_line:"*/i:*" and process.command_line:"*http*"))
query_kql: (process.executable.caseless:*\\rundll32.exe AND (process.command_line:(*javascript\:* OR *http\:\/\/* OR *https\:\/\/*))) OR (process.executable.caseless:*\\regsvr32.exe AND (process.command_line:*\/i\:* AND process.command_line:*http*))

title: SSH Authorized Keys Modified
description: Detects writes to SSH authorized_keys. A new public key gives an attacker persistent access without knowing a password.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Users adding their own key through an approved workflow

title: Shadow Copy Deletion via VSSAdmin or WMIC
description: Detects deletion of volume shadow copies, a common step before ransomware encryption because it removes the fastest local recovery path.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Backup software that rotates shadow copies
query: any where (process.executable.caseless:"*\\vssadmin.exe" and process.command_line:"*delete*" and process.command_line:"*shadows*") or (process.executable.caseless:"*\\wmic.exe" and (process.command_line:"*shadowcopy*" and process.command_line:"*delete*")) or (process.command_line:"*Win32_ShadowCopy*" and process.command_line:"*Delete*")
query_kql: (process.executable.caseless:*\\vssadmin.exe AND process.command_line:*delete* AND process.command_line:*shadows*) OR (process.executable.caseless:*\\wmic.exe AND (process.command_line:*shadowcopy* AND process.command_line:*delete*)) OR (process.command_line:*Win32_ShadowCopy* AND process.command_line:*Delete*)

title: Sudoers File Modified
description: Detects writes to sudoers files. An attacker with root can add a persistent privilege escalation path that survives password changes.
author: Meruyert

title: Suspicious Service Installed From User-Writable Path
description: Detects a new Windows service whose binary lives in a user-writable directory or launches through a shell interpreter. This is a common persistence mechanism after initial access.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Legitimate software installers that stage files in ProgramData or Temp
Updaters that run a service from a user profile
query: any where winlog.channel:"System" and (event.code:"7045" and (winlog.event_data.ImagePath like~ ("*\\Users\\Public\\*", "*\\AppData\\*", "*\\Temp\\*", "*\\ProgramData\\*", "*cmd.exe /c*", "*powershell*")) and (not (winlog.event_data.ServiceName like~ ("WaaSMedicSvc", "BITS", "WinDefend"))))
query_kql: winlog.channel:System AND (winlog.channel:System AND (event.code:7045 AND (winlog.event_data.ImagePath:(*\\Users\\Public\\* OR *\\AppData\\* OR *\\Temp\\* OR *\\ProgramData\\* OR *cmd.exe\ \/c* OR *powershell*)) AND (NOT (winlog.event_data.ServiceName:(WaaSMedicSvc OR BITS OR WinDefend)))))

title: Systemd Service Unit Created
description: Detects a new systemd unit in a system directory. Attackers use services for persistence and to restart payloads after reboot.
author: Meruyert

title: UAC Bypass via Auto-Elevating Binary
description: Detects known auto-elevating Windows binaries spawning a shell. These binaries run at high integrity without a prompt and are common UAC bypass hosts.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Legacy applications that use these binaries as launchers
query_kql: (process.parent.executable.caseless:(*\\fodhelper.exe OR *\\eventvwr.exe OR *\\sdclt.exe OR *\\computerdefaults.exe)) AND (process.executable.caseless:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe))

title: WMI Event Subscription Persistence
description: Detects creation of WMI event filters and consumers, a fileless persistence method that survives reboot and is invisible to Run key checks.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Monitoring agents that register WMI subscriptions

title: Windows Defender Real-Time Protection Disabled
description: Detects Windows Defender events indicating real-time protection, behaviour monitoring or tamper protection was disabled. Ransomware and commodity loaders routinely disable Defender before payload execution.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Endpoint management tools that temporarily disable protection during upgrades
query: any where winlog.channel:"Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational" and (event.code like~ ("5001", "5010", "5012"))
query_kql: winlog.channel:"Microsoft\-Windows\-Windows Defender\/Operational" AND (winlog.channel:"Microsoft\-Windows\-Windows Defender\/Operational" AND (event.code:(5001 OR 5010 OR 5012)))

title: Windows Event Log Cleared
description: Detects clearing of the Security event log. This destroys the record an analyst needs most, and it is rare in normal operations.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Audit log rotation performed by an administrator
Host imaging or lab reset scripts

title: DNS Query to Exfiltration Domain
description: Detects DNS queries for names under a domain used by the lab exfiltration scenario. The correlation layer escalates repeated long queries into a tunnel alert.
author: Meruyert

title: Data Staged with Archive Utility
description: Detects command-line archiving into a user-writable path. Attackers collect documents into one archive before exfiltration.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Users creating archives for legitimate backup
query: any where process.command_line like~ ("*rar a *", "*7z a *", "*Compress-Archive*", "*makecab *")
query_kql: process.command_line:(*rar\ a\ * OR *7z\ a\ * OR *Compress\-Archive* OR *makecab\ *)

title: New Local User Account Created
description: Detects useradd creating a new local account, as recorded by the auth log. Attackers create accounts to retain access after the initial vector is closed.
author: Meruyert

title: Path Traversal Attempt in Web Request
description: Detects directory traversal sequences in the URL path or query. Successful traversal exposes files outside the web root.
author: Meruyert

title: SQL Injection Attempt in Web Request
description: Detects common SQL injection payloads in query strings. A single request is a probe; repeated attempts from one source are escalated by correlation.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Security scanners and application penetration tests
Legacy applications that send SQL-like text in parameters
query: any where url.query like~ ("*union select*", "*' or 1=1*", "*sleep(*", "*benchmark(*", "*information_schema*")
query_kql: url.query:(*union\ select* OR *'\ or\ 1\=1* OR *sleep\(* OR *benchmark\(* OR *information_schema*)

title: Scheduled Task Created via Schtasks
description: Detects schtasks.exe creating a new scheduled task from a non-system account. Scheduled tasks are a durable, low-noise persistence and execution mechanism.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Software installers and updaters that register scheduled tasks
query: any where process.executable.caseless:"*\\schtasks.exe" and process.command_line:"*/create*" and (not user.name:"*$")

title: Web Request to Common Web Shell Parameter
description: Detects requests carrying command execution parameters frequently used by PHP and JSP web shells (cmd=, exec=, shell=). Complements the upload rule by catching interaction with a shell that was planted earlier.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Administrative panels that legitimately use cmd or exec parameters

title: Windows Firewall Disabled
description: Detects commands that turn off Windows Firewall profiles. Attackers disable the firewall before installing remote access or moving laterally.
author: Meruyert
falsepositives: Endpoint management tools that temporarily disable a profile
query: any where ((process.command_line:"*advfirewall*" and process.command_line:"*set*") and (process.command_line like~ ("*off*", "*disable*"))) or (process.command_line:"*Set-NetFirewallProfile*" and process.command_line:"*Enabled*" and process.command_line:"*False*")
query_kql: ((process.command_line:*advfirewall* AND process.command_line:*set*) AND (process.command_line:(*off* OR *disable*))) OR (process.command_line:*Set\-NetFirewallProfile* AND process.command_line:*Enabled* AND process.command_line:*False*)

title: Host and Account Discovery Command
description: Detects individual discovery commands that map the local host, domain, or user context. Volume is escalated by the discovery correlation, so the base rule stays low noise.
author: Meruyert
query: any where process.command_line like~ ("*whoami*", "*net user*", "*net group*", "*net view*", "*nltest*", "*systeminfo*", "*ipconfig /all*")
query_kql: process.command_line:(*whoami* OR *net\ user* OR *net\ group* OR *net\ view* OR *nltest* OR *systeminfo* OR *ipconfig\ \/all*)

title: SSH Failed Password Authentication
description: Matches individual failed SSH password attempts. This is intentionally a single-event rule: volume-based escalation (brute force) is handled by the correlation layer in pipeline/correlate.py so the base rule stays portable across SIEMs that do not support threshold aggregations.
author: Meruyert

title: Web Scanner User Agent
description: Detects user agents associated with common vulnerability scanners. This is reconnaissance, not exploitation, so the base rule stays low severity.
author: Meruyert
query_kql: user_agent.original:(*sqlmap* OR *nikto* OR *nmap* OR *masscan* OR *gobuster* OR *dirbuster*)
